title: Orbital Discreteness Modulates Electron-Counting Adsorption Trends in Atomically Dispersed Catalysts
abstract: Understanding adsorption at atomically dispersed catalytic sites remains a central challenge, as conventional d-band theory fails to describe emerging molecular-like electronic structures in single-atom systems. Here, we identify a unified electronic framework that bridges metallic single-atom alloys and nitrogen-coordinated graphene single-atom catalysts (transition-metal atoms coordinated by four nitrogen atoms in graphene, TM-N4-Gr), connecting band-like and ligand-field-dominated regimes through a common orbital-filling picture.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Magid Abou-Gharbia wins 2026 John Scott Award
abstract: The ACS member is recognized for his help developing drugs to treat depression, pain, and cancer

title: Systematic Improvement of Trial States in Phaseless Auxiliary-Field Quantum Monte Carlo
abstract: We extend the use of coupled cluster (CC) trial states in the phaseless auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (AFQMC) method beyond single and double excitations to include both triple and quadruple excitations. With this AFQMC/CC hierarchy, we are able to systematically benchmark the method’s performance on molecular systems as the quality of the trial is improved. Our results show that the phaseless AFQMC energy improves systematically and is typically significantly more accurate than the energy of the underlying trial state.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: How the CIA tried to use chemistry to kill Castro—and why it failed
abstract: The agency explored toxins, hallucinogens, and other chemical tricks to kill or discredit the Cuban leader. But the science behind the schemes often fell short of the agency’s ambitions

title: Water-Cluster-Expanded Interpenetrated Covalent Organic Frameworks Create High-Affinity Coordination Microenvironments for Efficient Strontium Capture
abstract: The efficient capture of radioactive strontium (Sr2+) from nuclear-contaminated water is of critical importance for environmental safety and public health protection. Three-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (3D COFs) with multi-interpenetrated architectures offer the potential for multidentate synergistic coordination toward target Sr2+. However, the confined internal environment arising from uncontrolled multi-interpenetration often restricts coordination freedom, while the concomitant reduction in pore size and obstruction of transport channels impose significant kinetic limitations…
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Model systems and integration strategies to capture human biology
abstract: Predictive human-relevant model systems are outlined in a Review by integrating engineered materials and microenvironments, human tissue and organ models, computational approaches, and closed-loop strategies. Controlling the boundary conditions, biological organization, measurements and model calibration can improve mechanistic insight, reproducibility and translational relevance across applications.

title: Reordering of Retinal Reactions Underlies Reversal of Proton-Pump Directionality
abstract: Light-driven proton-pumping rhodopsins transport protons either outward or inward across membranes, but the molecular determinants of transport vectoriality remain unclear. An outward proton-pumping rhodopsin from Pseudomonas putida (PspR) was previously converted into an inward pump by substituting only three amino acid residues. Here, time-resolved resonance Raman spectroscopy reveals that wild-type PspR accepts a proton with a 13-cis retinal chromophore, whereas the engineered inward-pumping PspR triple mutant accepts a proton with an all-trans chromophore, as observed in schizorhodopsins.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Scalable physical deep learning using optical dynamics with state-skipping training and single-map architecture
abstract: This study presents a scalable, efficient framework for unconventional computing with physical neural networks. It replaces dense connections with uncoupled one-dimensional dynamics, simplifies training, improves performance and reduces resource use.

title: Lipidic α-synuclein fibrils catalyze the formation of pathological mature fibrils
abstract: The aggregation of -synuclein into amyloid fibrils is a hallmark of a collection of neurodegenerative diseases termed synucleinopathies, including Parkinson's disease (PD). Interactions between -synuclein and lipid membranes modulate -synuclein aggregation and can produce protofibril structures consisting of both protein and lipid, termed lipidic fibrils. These lipidic fibrils can mature into mature fibrils, which resemble ex vivo fibrils extracted from Lewy bodies found in post-mortem brain samples of PD patients.

title: Translating chemical reactions into enzyme sequences enables formate dehydrogenase engineering
abstract: Enzyme engineering has broad applications across chemistry and biotechnology but remains costly and susceptible to low success rates. Generative artificial intelligence can substantially expand the sequence space accessible to enzyme engineering; however, directing generation towards enzymes that catalyse a user-defined chemical reaction remains challenging. Inspired by machine translation, we formulate enzyme generation as translation between two molecular languages: chemical reactions and amino acid sequences. Here, we introduce REXzyme, a translation model that generates enzymes conditioned on user-defined reactions. First, we evaluate its designs using multiple in silico metrics and characterize the strengths and limitations of its generalisation capacity. Then, we steer REXzyme towards the generation of enhanced formate dehydrogenases for their reverse natural reaction, i.e., the reduction of carbon dioxide. All 20 generated enzymes were expressed and purified as soluble proteins and exhibited CO2-reduction activity, with the most active design reaching 2.5-fold the specific activity of the reference enzyme. Notably, all substitutions in the designed variants were performed on distal positions outside the catalytic site. Our results show that reaction-to-sequence translation provides a route for efficiently engineering enhanced biocatalysts.

title: The binding landscape of Ras/effector interactions provides insights on Ras switching and oncogenesis
abstract: Protein-protein interactions (PPIs) regulate essential cellular processes, yet the evolutionary principles that shape their specificity, adaptability, and dysregulation in disease remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate the evolution of a signaling PPI between the small GTPase Ras and its effector Nore1A, a tumor suppressor involved in Ras-mediated signaling. Ras acts as a molecular switch, engaging effectors in its GTP-bound active state and releasing them after GTP hydrolysis, whereas oncogenic mutations such as G12D lock Ras in the active state, promoting aberrant signaling in cancer. Using yeast surface display, deep mutational scanning, and data normalization, we systematically mapped the Ras/Nore1A binding landscape under different physiological and oncogenic states. We generated and screened $\sim$33,000 Nore1A single and double mutants against RasWT and RasG12D in both GTP- and GDP-bound states. Our data revealed that most Nore1A mutations produce small-to-moderate decrease in Ras affinity, while a small number of substitutions enhance affinity. Unexpectedly, GTP hydrolysis causes minimal remodeling of the interaction landscape. Conversely, the oncogenic RasG12D mutation reshapes the binding landscape, revealing many Nore1A variants with enhanced and selective affinity for mutant Ras. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of Nore1A-Ras variant complexes suggest that the non-optimality of the Nore1A/RasG12D binding landscape arises, in part, from the greater intrinsic flexibility of RasG12D and the pronounced reduction in flexibility induced by affinity-enhancing Nore1A mutations. These findings demonstrate that disease-associated mutations can create new evolutionary trajectories in signaling PPIs by changing interaction dynamics and provide a framework for engineering selective protein-based inhibitors targeting oncogenic Ras variants.

title: Multi-objective domain adaptation for pan-cancer transfer of pharmacogenomic drug response to patient tumours
abstract: Large-scale pharmacogenomic screens provide rich drug-sensitivity measurements in cancer cell lines, but transferring these measurements to patient tumours remains limited by biological heterogeneity and cross-domain distribution shift. Existing machine learning approaches, including adversarial autoencoder and domain adaptation, address this gap by learning shared latent representations between preclinical models and patient samples.

title: Growth-driven mechanical buckling as a mechanism of age-related tortuosity in human cerebral arteries
abstract: Human cerebral arteries become increasingly, sometimes abnormally, winding with age, but the mechanical basis of this change remains incompletely understood. To examine how arterial bends form and what sets their spacing, we modeled a cerebral artery as a slender elastic vessel supported by surrounding tissue. The distance between its ends remains constant, and the vessel can bend only in a plane tangent to the brain surface. As its natural length increases, axial compression builds until the vessel buckles. Bending partly relieves the compression, and the resulting waves grow in amplitude as elongation continues. Arterial bending stiffness and tissue support determine the wavelength, which is much larger than and proportional to vessel diameter, with comparatively weak dependence on other parameters. Numerical simulations captured a pre-buckling phase, rapid amplification of waves, and slow post-buckling growth during continued elongation. We evaluated these predictions using three-dimensional centerlines of cerebral arteries reconstructed from magnetic resonance angiography in healthy adults. Older age was associated with greater arterial length and excess-length ratio. For arterial waves oriented mostly parallel to the brain surface, wavelength increased with vessel diameter. Both this relationship and the observed wavelength-to-diameter ratio were consistent with model predictions. However, wave amplitude was not significantly associated with age. Overall, the modeling and imaging results support growth-driven buckling and post-buckling deformation under spatial constraint as a plausible mechanical explanation for age-related cerebral arterial tortuosity. This framework links vascular aging to growth-driven instability and pattern formation, with potential applications to diseased arteries beyond the brain.

title: Autonomous Agricultural Robot Framework featuring Temporal Dynamic Graph Neural Network based Semantic Segmentation coupled with Novel Navigation Line Extraction for efficient field operation and intelligent decision making
abstract: BackgroundAutonomous agricultural robots support precision farming and improve operational efficiency; however, reliable navigation in complex field environments remains challenging because of inconsistent lighting, variable soil textures, irregular crop growth patterns, and visual occlusions. These conditions hinder accurate crop row detection, semantic segmentation, and navigation line extraction.

title: Transition Metal Chalcogenides as Electrocatalysts for Anion Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis
abstract: Amid escalating energy demand and severe environmental effects, green hydrogen production via water electrolysis has emerged as a cornerstone technology. Conventional alkaline water electrolysis (AWE) generally suffers from low hydrogen purity and current density, while proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) relies on high-cost noble-metal catalysts and harsh acidic conditions.

title: A Three-Level Noise Floor for Cyclodextrin Binding Constants and What It Permits for Descriptor-Based Prediction
abstract: Regression and machine-learning models for cyclodextrin inclusion constants are often reported with cross-validated Q2 near 0.9, yet the reproducibility of the compiled data on which they are trained has not been quantified. This work quantifies it at three levels, each defined by the uncertainty it captures. The within-experiment fitting precision of a single calorimetric study, 0.008 log units, is a lower bound on repeatability; head-to-head comparisons between laboratories and methods give 0.115 log units (95% CI: 0.079–0.210); and 128 replicated host–guest pairs in a verified extraction…
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Researchers develop synergistic additives for scalable slot-die-coated perovskite photovoltaics
abstract: A research team led by Professor Yang Dong from the Dalian Institute of Chemical Physics (DICP) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS), in collaboration with Dalian Jiaotong University, has developed a synergistic additive strategy for large-area slot-die coating of methylammonium-free (MA-free) perovskite films. The study is published in Advanced Materials.

title: From Classification Accuracy to Decision Value: Multimodal Sensor Fusion for Economic Prioritization of Landfill Mining Simulation-based Value-of-Information Analysis
abstract: Landfill mining projects are approved or shelved on incomplete information about what is underground, and a systematic assessment of European scenarios revealed that approximately 19% of them are profitable [1]. In this paper, by simulation, whether multimodal geophysical sensing combined with spatial machine learning and value-of-information (VOI) analysis can reduce that uncertainty before excavation is evaluated.

title: A plant-based hair dye that smells like cinnamon
abstract: Hair dyes help people express style and cover gray hair but often contain skin-irritating chemicals.

title: Discovery of One-Dimensional Rare-Earth Hybrid Nitrate Double Perovskites
abstract: Rare-earth hybrid nitrate double perovskites (REHNDPs) have recently emerged as an intriguing subclass of functional materials, combining structural diversity with rich intrinsic optoelectronic, magnetic, piezoelectric, and ferroelectric properties. Although notable progress has been made in three-dimensional (3D) and 2D REHNDPs, 1D counterparts have yet to be discovered. Herein, by introducing the bulky organic cation 1-adamantyltrimethylammonium (TMAA+), we report a family of 1D REHNDPs with the general formula (TMAA)2LnCs(NO3)6 (Ln = La3+, Ce3+, Pr3+, Nd3+, Sm3+, and Eu3+).

title: Three-Dimensional Hollow Square Array SAPO-34 with Optimal Acidity Distribution Showing Excellent Methanol-to-Olefins Performance
abstract: SAPO-34 is an excellent catalyst for methanol-to-olefins (MTO) reaction. Simultaneously alleviating the diffusion limitations and optimizing the acidity of SAPO-34 is extremely challenging. Herein, a three-dimensional hollow square array SAPO-34 (SAPO-34-HSA) with a sinusoidal-like distribution of silicon was synthesized in a simple way. The role of triethylamine (TEA) switches between the etchant and structure-directing agent according to the reaction temperature.

title: Scientists discover that a clogged filter could revolutionize oil refining
abstract: Scientists have developed a remarkable new membrane that separates crude oil at room temperature, using the oil itself to create microscopic filtration channels. The breakthrough could cut refining energy consumption by nearly 32%, carbon emissions by almost 38%, and operating costs by 36%, potentially transforming one of the world's most energy-intensive industries.

title: TRPP Ion Channels Function in the π-Conformation Rather Than the α-Conformation
abstract: PKD2 (TRPP1) is a TRPP ion channel whose dysfunction causes autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD). Understanding its conformational states and gating mechanism is important for elucidating its function and for structure-based drug discovery. Cryo-EM structures of WT-PKD2 contain a local {pi}-helical turn in the S6 pore-lining helix ({pi}-conformation). In contrast, a fully -helical S6 (-conformation) was observed in the gain-of-function mutant F604P-PKD2 and interpreted as the open state, leading to the proposed {pi}-to- activation mechanism. However, whether the -conformation can support function has never been directly established. Here, using molecular dynamics simulations, we investigate the functional properties of the -and {pi}-conformations of PKD2. The -conformation remains dewetted unless the lower gate is widened beyond the conformational range observed in mammalian TRP channels. By contrast, the {pi}-conformation supports pore hydration and ion conduction following a small opening of the L677 gate, with simulated conductance comparable to experimental measurements. The closely related PKD2L1 (TRPP2) channel shows a similar dependence on conformation, with a hydrated {pi}-conformation and a dewetted -conformation. Together, these findings challenge the assignment of the -conformation as the conductive state and support a model in which the {pi}-conformation represents the functionally relevant state of TRPP channels. This model suggests that activation may involve an -to-{pi} transition rather than the previously proposed {pi}-to- transition, providing a new framework for understanding TRPP channel gating. This work sheds light on the molecular basis of polycystin channel dysfunction and could facilitate the development of PKD2-targeted therapeutic strategies for ADPKD.

title: Wheat kernels analyzed for better bread
abstract: Scientists use near-infrared spectroscopy and artificial intelligence to predict which wheat breeds make the best loaves

title: Ultralow Pt-Loaded Pt/Fe2O3 with Pt−Fe Pair Sites for Efficient Seawater Hydrogen Production
abstract: Seawater electrolysis for green hydrogen production urgently demands high-performance electrocatalysts that simultaneously deliver fast reaction kinetics with robust chloride ion (Cl−) resistance. Herein, we report an ultralow Pt-loaded (<1 wt %) Pt/Fe2O3 catalyst rich in Pt−Fe atomic pairs synthesized via a photoreduction synthetic strategy. Photogenerated electrons drive the selective reduction of Pt precursors at low-coordinate Fe3+ sites on α-Fe2O3 (012) facets, constructing Pt−Fe pair interfaces that enable directional electron transfer from Fe-dz2 to Pt-dz2 orbitals.

title: How cellophane bees make a plastic that doesn’t pile up
abstract: Solitary bees line their nests with a polyester that degrades within months, hinting at design rules for biodegradable plastics

title: Emergent Structural Prototypes of Stable Inorganic Materials
abstract: The number of possible crystal structures vastly exceeds the number realized among thermodynamically stable inorganic materials, suggesting that experimentally accessible structure space is organized around a limited set of preferred structural frameworks. Analysis of 23,160 structures on the thermodynamic convex hull identifies 6820 distinct structural frameworks, of which 2382 recur across multiple chemically distinct materials and are therefore classified as structural prototypes. Within a filtered dataset, metallic systems exhibit particularly strong structural recurrence, with 6270 materials grouped into 535 frameworks and 327 prototypes, while 5557 ionic compounds occupy 1704 frameworks and 696 prototypes. These results demonstrate that stable inorganic materials naturally coalesce into recurrent structural prototypes and do not require any a priori definition through manual curation. The resulting recurrence-based catalog also provides an empirical measure of framework prevalence, enabling the relative likelihood of structural frameworks in future materials to be estimated from their recurrence among known compounds.

title: A phenanthrene co-guest helps crystalline sponges reveal 3D structures of small, low-polarity molecules
abstract: Adding phenanthrene as a co-guest let the second-generation crystalline sponge (2G-CS) method determine X-ray structures for 24 of 30 small, low-polarity C₁₅ molecules, mostly sesquiterpenoids. Under standard conditions, none of the 30 gave guest-containing crystals. Eleven of the 24 structures had not been reported before, including that of the liquid hydrocarbon longifolene. A chiral version of the cage gave the absolute configurations of five compounds.

title: Bioinformatic-Guided Discovery of O -Dealkylation Activity in Cytochrome P450 Monooxygenases
abstract: The O-dealkylation of alkyl ethers—or the removal of small alkyl protecting groups (PGs)—remains a significant challenge in organic synthesis. While traditional chemical methods require harsh reaction conditions and lack sufficient selectivity, biocatalytic approaches represent valuable alternatives. However, enzymes facilitating the desired O-dealkylation reactions are scarce. In this work, we applied a sequence similarity network (SSN)-guided approach to identify cytochrome P450 monooxygenases (CYPs) with O-dealkylation activity within the growing sequence diversity found in public databases. We investigated six CYPs, three of which exhibited significant activity toward structurally diverse ethers bearing methyl, ethyl, propyl, or allyl groups. While P450ThcB and P450Terp enabled the deprotection of aromatic and aliphatic primary and secondary ethers, P450Sca2-mut complemented the substrate scope by effectively deprotecting sterically demanding tertiary ethers. In particular, P450ThcB and P450Terp exhibited high regioselectivity, preferentially cleaving phenolic over benzylic ethers. Furthermore, P450ThcB enabled the regioselective deprotection of veratryl alcohol. Preparative scale reactions of three substrates yielded up to 74% of the isolated and (regioselectively) cleaved alcohol product. Together, these findings substantially expand the enzymatic toolbox for the selective removal of alkyl PGs and highlight the suitability of SSN-guided database mining approaches for the identification of biocatalysts with the desired function.

title: Integrative miRNA-multi-omics analysis of brain-metastasis predisposition in non-small cell lung cancer prioritizes HDAC inhibitors and anti-miR-330-3p as hypothesis-generating therapeutic candidates
abstract: Brain metastasis (BM) is the leading cause of death in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet its molecular drivers remain poorly targeted. Here we present an integrative in-silico pipeline that moves from miRNA discovery to therapeutic hypothesis generation. Reprocessing the GSE23019 miRNA microarray cohort (7 BM+ versus 5 BM- primary tumors) recovered the published BM-associated miRNAs miR-328 and miR-330-3p and, through validated miRNA-target interactions, yielded a signature of 828 up-regulated and 177 down-regulated genes enriched for extracellular-matrix and vasculature programs.

title: A timeline for evolution of metabolism in early microbes
abstract: The metabolism of early microbes shaped our planet's chemistry and enabled more life to evolve. However, it remains uncertain when many forms of metabolism arose and which organisms carried them out. Here we combine machine learning, metabolic networks, and phylogenomics of microbes to date 14 forms of metabolism and 6 other traits. We find that metabolism evolved in three waves, starting >3.4 billion years ago (Ga) with fermentation and sulfur compound respiration. A second wave began ~3.2 Ga with aerobic respiration and growth, while a third began ~1.4 Ga with further specialization.

title: A Binuclear Cluster Supports Functional Asymmetry in Dark-Operative Protochlorophyllide Reductase
abstract: Many photosynthetic bacteria rely on the nitrogenase-like dark-operative protochlorophyllide oxidoreductase (DPOR) to sustain (bacterio)chlorophyll synthesis in the dark. DPOR couples ATP hydrolysis to electron transfer from a reducing component (L-protein) to a catalytic component (NB-protein) that reduces protochlorophyllide. NB-protein is an 2{beta}2 heterotetramer, and each heterodimeric half contains an active site and a [Fe4S4] cluster. Although the two halves are identical, they react sequentially rather than in parallel. How the two halves communicate has remained unknown. Here we show, using Cu K-edge x-ray absorption spectroscopy and cryo-EM, that the NB-protein tetramer interface holds a binuclear, sulfur-bridged [Cu2S2] cluster. Each Cu is reduced and three-coordinate, with short Cu-S and Cu-Cu distances (2.26 and 2.62 &Aring). Mutagenesis excludes the nearest cysteine as the bridging ligand, supporting inorganic sulfide as the most likely sulfur donor. To our knowledge, this is the first sulfide-bridged dicopper cluster identified in a protein. The cluster is conserved in three purple non-sulfur bacteria and connects the BchB C-terminal helices that contact opposing active sites. Loss of Cu abolishes DPOR activity and asymmetric L-protein binding without disturbing overall fold. We propose that the cluster relays substrate-binding information between active sites, suggesting a metal-mediated mechanism for cooperativity in nitrogenase-like enzymes.

title: Cathode-Induced Stress Can Suppress Dendritic Failure in Thin Solid Electrolyte Separators
abstract: Solid-state batteries pairing lithium metal anodes with inorganic solid electrolytes promise a step change in energy density, but during charging at practical rates lithium dendrites penetrate the solid electrolyte, short-circuiting the cell. Our current understanding of dendrite propagation derives largely from symmetric Li−Li cells with millimetre-thick electrolyte pellets, whereas practical cells will employ solid electrolyte separators less than 100 μm in thickness. In this work, we use in situ synchrotron X-ray computed tomography to show that dendrites in a thin Li6PS5Cl separator, which generally propagate from the lithium anode to the cathode, can be made to propagate laterally by the cathode. Volume contraction of the NMC cathode during charge places the thin separator under lateral compressive stress, deflecting dendritic cracks to propagate laterally (parallel to the electrodes) rather than transversely (across the separator). The result is that the cell resists short circuit even after passing 3 mA h cm−2 capacity at a rate of 3 mA cm−2. Replacing NMC with zero-volume-change pre-lithiated Li4Ti5O12 removes this compressive stress, and the cell rapidly fails by transverse cracking. Chemomechanical modelling rationalises both behaviours, with cathode volume change emerging as a design parameter that can suppress or accelerate failure, with direct implications for cathode selection and cathode/separator interface engineering in practical solid-state batteries.

title: Geometry-Programmed Connectivity Enables Predictive Assembly of Diamond-Family Colloidal Crystals
abstract: The predictive assembly of open colloidal crystals requires encoding specific connectivity rules into building blocks that are otherwise isotropic and lack inherent directionality. Here we introduce a geometry-programmed connectivity strategy in which spatial confinement, rather than surface patterning or lattice templating, programs not only particle coordination but also the accessible bonding arrangement that governs network connectivity.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: FROST III: certified Hartree–Fock limits of diatomic molecules
abstract: We extend FROST (Fock radial orbital shooting with Taylor series) from atoms to diatomic molecules and obtain the Hartree–Fock (HF) energy of H2 at the internuclear distance R = 1.4 bohr to 103 significant figures, that of HeH+ to 101 and that of LiH to 26, each certified by an exact upper bound, where about 11, 9 and 12 figures were known before. In prolate spheroidal coordinates both nuclear cusps are absorbed and the nuclear attraction becomes linear.

title: Active Learning for Fragment-Based Kinase Inhibitor Discovery using Docking
abstract: Drug discovery requires efficient exploration of vast chemical spaces while minimizing computational cost. Fragment-based drug design offers a promising route for generating novel ligands through recombination of fragments, yet the resulting combinatorial search spaces rapidly become too large for exhaustive evaluation. Here, we present an active learning framework for navigating kinase-focused fragment recombination spaces derived from KinFragLib.

title: Encapsulation of f-block elements in borocarbide cages: Synthesis of a magnetic NdB3C3 clathrate
abstract: We report the synthesis of a boron–carbon clathrate with neodymium guest ions, which is stabilized under high-pressure conditions and recoverable to ambient pressure. The compound, NdB3C3, crystallizes in the bipartite sodalite structure (space group Pm3̄n), as determined by single-crystal X-ray diffraction, and exhibits a zero-pressure bulk modulus K0 = 252(12) GPa. The electronic and magnetic properties of NdB3C3 were investigated using density functional theory with PBE, PBEsol, the HSE06 hybrid exchange–correlation functional, and DFT+U .

title: Landfill methane recovery and use under deep uncertainty: a satelliteconstrained Monte Carlo decision model for the Norte III landfill, Buenos Aires
abstract: Very large landfills are major methane sources, but site decisions rarely join operator-reported capture, independent emission estimates and the economics of competing gas uses. We built a Latin-hypercube Monte Carlo decision model (300,000 draws, 78 inputs) of landfill-gas generation, collection, surface emission, oxidation, selective covers, biomethane upgrading, additional power generation and photovoltaics, and applied it to the Norte III landfill in Buenos Aires. A bottom-up generation prior is constrained by satellite emission estimates at their own date (2022) and carried to 2025–26.

title: Mass-Constrained Integration of Cryogenic Propellant Management and Carbon–Hydrogen–Oxygen Resource Recovery for Mars Surface Depots: A Monte Carlo Feasibility Study
abstract: A Mars surface propellant depot must make methane and oxygen, liquefy them and keep them cold on a limited launch mass, and each kilogram of added hardware displaces a kilogram of imported feedstock. This study asks which added layers pay for their mass. Seven nested depot configurations are compared at equal launch masses (9 t, a 30 kW array, 3 t of methane and 10.5 t of oxygen storage) by Monte Carlo simulation of 33 uncertain parameters, with paired comparisons and an independent energy audit.

title: A Doubly Reversible Covalent Adaptable Network for (A)Cellular 3D Manufacturing and Post-Culture Cell Retrieval
abstract: Covalent adaptable networks (CANs) are polymer networks in which bond formation and cleavage occur dynamically and reversibly. They are intensively investigated for 3D cell culture, as they model a more physiologically representative environment than traditional 2D culture. In most 3D matrices, however, cell retrieval for downstream analysis remains limited, and overcoming this limitation would advance in vitro 3D models for biomedical research.

title: Accurate and Rapid Vibrational Spectra of Molecular Crystals from Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials
abstract: Currently, vibrational spectra of molecular crystals often require computational methods to aid in band assignment, especially in the low-frequency region where no functional group specific transitions exist. DFT methods are the gold-standard for computational spectroscopy, but their high computational cost limits simulations to systems characterized by small unit cells. Universal machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) offer a much cheaper alternative, but their reliability for phonons in molecular crystals has been little explored.

title: The Copper(I)-catalyzed Alkyne-azide Cycloaddition “Click” Reaction in Water Requires the Formation of Two Distinct Mononuclear Copper(I) Complexes
abstract: The copper-catalyzed azide-alkyne cycloaddition (CuAAC) has seen widespread adoption amongst numerous fields, but mechanistic details remain elusive and controversial. Using a series of experiments involving fluorogenic coumarin derivatives under pseudo-first order conditions, it was determined that the reaction in conditions close to a physiological environment does not proceed according to the accepted mechanism, but rather requires azide chelation to form a mononuclear copper(I)-azide complex as a preliminary step.

title: Applicability Domain of Universal Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials at Solid-State Battery Interfaces
abstract: Universal machine learning interatomic potentials (uMLIPs) are trained predominantly on bulk systems, yet are increasingly applied to solid-solid interfaces. Evaluating six uMLIPs against DFT across 24 Li-metal/solid-electrolyte interfaces, we map their applicability domain (AD) and where they break down. Total energies are predicted reasonably well (MAE < 15 meV/atom), whereas interatomic forces at the interfaces are not.

title: AuditRxn: Auditable Fast-Weight Memories for Multi-Step Chemical Reaction Prefix-Prediction
abstract: Multi-step organic synthesis planning requires tracking dynamic molecular transformations, protecting groups, and reaction conditions across sequential chemical stages. Existing chemical language models treat multi-step reaction sequences as flattened token streams within standard autoregressive Transformers. Under this paradigm, context lengths grow quadratically, low-information solvents and auxiliary reagents dilute attention away from reactive transformation centers, and hidden state transitions remain uninterpretable black boxes that hallucinate physically impossible steps violating…

title: Sharp Bounds for Raman Band-Area Ratios
abstract: Nonnegative signal and background components, bounded observational error, constraints on background smoothness and band-free anchor measurements define a set of admissible decompositions. Linear-fractional optimization gives the exact minimum and maximum band ratios over this set, while a feasibility problem tests consistency of the imposed constraints. A closed-form bound relates remaining area uncertainty to the anchor spacing, background curvature, noise and band profile.

title: Lost in Chemical Space: Local Open-Source Large Language Models Display Model-Dependent Adherence to Reference Data in Molecular Generation
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can generate drug-like molecules and may be used locally in drug discovery projects where confidentiality and intellectual-property constraints preclude the use of external APIs. Weight quantization enables deployment of large open-source LLMs on limited hardware, but its impact on molecular generation and on the ability of models to follow reference chemical spaces remains poorly understood.

title: POLEN: An OpenMM Framework for ML/MM Simulations with Mutually Polarizable AMOEBA Embedding
abstract: Hybrid machine-learning and molecular mechanics formulations have been growing over the years. The attractive cost-effectiveness for big systems (such as protein complexes) has made these methods gain attention in the computational chemistry/biology field. In these theories, one of the most discussed themes is embedding, which can add or remove physics from the system.

title: Crystallographic Continuity Enables Programmable Living Biointerfaces
abstract: Dynamic biological entities are versatile but remain vulnerable to immune clearance, premature chemical exchange, and environmental degradation. Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) offer porous matrices for bioencapsulation; however, standard polycrystalline or nanoparticulate shells contain structural defects that compromise protective performance and molecular selectivity. Here, we demonstrate the complete encapsulation of viruses, bacteria, and mammalian erythrocytes within continuous single-crystalline ZIF-90 via biocompatible aqueous routes.

title: A reactor concept for more sustainable chemical vapor deposition of hard coatings
abstract: Chemical vapor deposition (CVD) is a key technology for producing hard coatings on cutting tools, but its sustainability is challenged by high energy consumption and low precursor utilization. We present a novel reactor concept for hard coating CVD inspired by spatial atomic layer deposition, aiming to reduce environmental impacts through minimized reactor volume, reduced thermal mass, and the possibility for precursor recirculation.

title: Sliding Window Attention with Auditable Chemical Sinks for Long-Sequence Molecular Transformation Modeling
abstract: Long molecular transformation sequences require models to track local bond changes and persistent reaction constraints. Conventional Transformers face high context costs, diluted attention, and chemically invalid predictions. We propose ChemSWA, an efficient and auditable framework for multi-step synthesis modeling. Adaptive Chemical Sliding Window Attention combines local windows with persistent attention sinks to retain reaction states at 𝑂 (𝑊 · 𝐿) computational complexity.

title: Isocyanide Ligand Tuning of Rhenium Imido N−H BDFE Values for Catalytic Dinitrogen Reduction
abstract: During N 2 reduction cycles that involve transition-metal-mediated N 2 splitting to nitrides, it is often thermodynamically difficult to form the first N–H bond on the way to ammonia. Increasing this N–H bond dissociation free energy (BDFE) is challenging because changes in the pK a and redox potential typically counteract one another. Here, we report that pincer-ligated rhenium complexes containing isocyanide ligands have dramatically higher imido N–H BDFE values than analogous chloride, cyanide, and pyridine complexes.

title: Copper-Catalyzed Enantioconvergent Synthesis of Sulfoxides from Racemic Sulfinate Esters and Organoboronic Acids
abstract: Chiral sulfoxides are important structural motifs in drug discovery and asymmetric synthesis. Transition-metalcatalyzed approaches to their enantioselective preparation have largely relied on thioether oxidation or coupling reactions involving highly reactive nucleophilic sulfinyl donors, such as sulfenic acids and sulfenate anions. Here, we report a copper-catalyzed enantioconvergent coupling of racemic sulfinate esters with organoboronic acids, in which the sulfinate esters serve as electrophilic sulfinyl donors.

title: Nucleophile-Stabilized Transient o-Quinodimethide Forges a Common Gateway Toward C-1 P/N/O/C-Substituted Tetrahydroisoquinolines
abstract: C-1-substituted tetrahydroisoquinolines (THIQs) represent a highly valuable and biologically privileged class of nitrogen heterocycles, owing to their stereochemically rich, structurally versatile scaffolds and widespread presence in medicinally relevant compounds, natural products, and bioactive molecules. Their remarkable pharmacological diversity and tunable molecular architecture make C-1-functionalized THIQs particularly powerful platforms for the discovery, design, and optimization of therapeutically important molecules.

title: Electrosynthesis of Free-Standing Polyoxometalate–PEDOT Hybrid Thin Films at a Polarizable Liquid|Liquid Interface
abstract: Polyoxometalates (POMs) are versatile molecular redox systems, yet their electrochemical behavior at polarizable liquid|liquid interfaces remains unexplored. Here, we investigate Keggin-type phosphomolybdic acid (PMA) and phosphotungstic acid (PTA) at a polarizable aqueous|α,α,α-trifluorotoluene interface and demonstrate their use as molecular oxidants and dopants for the interfacial electrosynthesis of free-standing POM-poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) (PEDOT) hybrid thin films.

title: Structural Analysis of HRF-4467, a Potent Second-Generation HIV-1 Maturation Inhibitor
abstract: HRF-4467 is a betulinic acid-derived HIV-1 maturation inhibitor that targets the canonical CA-SP1 region and blocks the final proteolytic step of viral maturation. Here, we characterize HRF-4467 and its para-fluoro analog using solution and solid-state NMR spectroscopy, supported by quantum-mechanical calculations. Using this approach, we established the molecular connectivity and conformation of HRF-4467 in solution and in the solid state.

title: Chemistry-Informed Transfer and Interaction-Resolved Learning Towards Data-Efficient Materials Exploration
abstract: Optimizing synthesis parameters for new thin-film materials is slow and often relies on intuition and trial and error. Gaussian process (GP) models suit low-data settings, but treat each material separately or need engineered descriptors to learn across materials. Multi-task GPs share information across materials but infer these relationships solely from sparse data, making them unreliable early on. We introduce a chemistry-informed multi-task GP that derives these relationships from a Tanimoto kernel on molecular fingerprints, enabling knowledge transfer without descriptor engineering.

title: 3D Structure Analysis from XAS using Diffusion Models
abstract: The local three-dimensional (3D) atomic structure of materials and molecules can be interrogated by X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES), a powerful analytical technique. Here, we introduce a diffusionmodel-based approach that rapidly infers candidate 3D structures from X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) data. The method is validated on multi-element hard X-ray XAS datasets and generalizes across a broad range of molecular and material systems without imposing restrictions on the number of constituent element types.

title: A Scoping Review of Diffusion-Based De Novo Molecular Generation: Architectures, Evaluation, and Open Challenges for Computational Drug Discovery
abstract: Diffusion models form the bulk of generative frameworks used in de novo molecular design, yet the literature remains fragmented across model formulations, molecular representations, and generative tasks, and inadequate systematic accounts exist of how these models are steered towards molecules with desired properties, an aspect of drug discovery that is paramount to acceptance. We present a scoping review of diffusion-based neural networks applied in de novo drug discovery between 2020 and 2026.

title: Facile Nitrogen Doping of Electrospun Mesoporous Carbon Nanofibers via Urea Addition for Polysulfide-Confining Li-S Cathodes and Interlayers
abstract: Lithium-sulfur (Li-S) batteries offer high theoretical capacity, but polysulfide dissolution and shuttling cause rapid capacity fade. Nitrogen functional groups can anchor polysulfides, yet in our previous work, introducing them through a post-carbonization cyclized-PAN treatment sacrificed much of the carbon nanofiber (CNF) mesoporosity, and Nfunctionalizing both cathode and interlayer performed worst. Here, nitrogen is introduced during fiber formation by adding urea to a PAN/PMMA precursor before gas-assisted electrospinning, followed by stabilization, carbonization, and CO2 activation.

title: C2 Homologation of Alkenes with Programmable Substitution
abstract: Alkene homologation represents an efficient strategy for upgrading commodity olefins and expediting the synthesis of their longer homologues. However, current alkene homologation methodologies are limited to the access to terminal alkenes. Herein, we report a radical‑based approach that enables C2 homologation of alkenes with programmable substitution patterns. This transformation features a radical hydro-alkylation of alkenes using bromomethylphosphonium hexafluorophosphate as an electrophilic carbon radical precursor.

title: Techno-Economic and Geospatial Assessment of Distributed Fertilizer Production via Wastewater Ammonia Solar Electrochemical Stripping
abstract: Decentralized alternatives to centralized fertilizer production are needed to reduce supply chain risks, minimize transportation costs, and lower environmental impacts. Solar-powered Electrochemical Stripping (ECS) is an emerging technology that can produce ammonium fertilizer in a distributed manner through wastewater nitrogen recovery. We quantify the fraction of fertilizer demand in the United States that can be met by a wastewater feedstock while minimizing transportation distances, finding that 55% (5.54 Mt N per year) of demand is co-located with sufficient supply from domestic…

title: Dynamical confinement effects on chromophore photoexcitations in a light-harvesting protein
abstract: Naturally evolved light-harvesting complexes are assembled from highly evolutionarily-conserved sequences of amino acids that form functional chemical pockets for chromophores. The protein environment surrounding the chromophore influences its dynamical structure, which can have consequences for light harvesting efficiency. Here, we explore the impact of the C-phycocyanin protein scaffold on the dynamical structure and photoexcited states of the phycocyanobilin (PCB) chromophore using a combination of molecular dynamics and the ab initio Bethe Salpeter equation approach.

title: Single-chirality single-walled carbon nanotubes for electrochemical co-detection of serotonin and dopamine
abstract: Dopamine (DA) and serotonin (5-HT) are neurotransmitters whose dysregulation is associated with neurodegenerative diseases. The influence of single-walled carbon nanotube (SWCNT) chirality on sensing remains underexplored. Mixed-chirality SWC- NTs can limit sensor reproducibility and accuracy. Precise control of electrode material structure may promote more specific surface-analyte interactions, enhancing selectivity.

title: Integration of Acoustic Ejection Mass Spectrometry Enables Efficient High Throughput Purification Workflow for Peptides in Discovery Space
abstract: 2 ABSTRACT Modern peptide drug discovery combines mRNA display-derived libraries and iterative optimization of hits using solid phase peptide synthesis (SPPS) during hit-to-lead process. Part of this discovery workflow is the need for sufficient amounts of high-quality peptide targets, free from impurities to support the required preclinical assays. In this context, there is a need for streamlined high throughput purification (HTP) workflow coupled with high throughput analytical assays, enabling faster analysis of large volumes of synthetic peptide libraries for purification to accelerate…

title: Recombination-zone position, not charge balance, sets the efficiency ceiling of deep-blue TADF host OLEDs
abstract: Low efficiency in organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) is often blamed on charge balance, yet the device models that could test this are rarely converged or constrained by measured inputs. We solve converged drift–diffusion, transfermatrix and dipole models for three deep-blue thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) phosphine-oxide hosts, S1, S3 and S4, with an open solver verified against a converged commercial reference, and we constrain every hostspecific input by measurement: film optical constants from ellipsometry, film photoluminescence, voltammetric host levels and host…

title: AI Agents as supporting infrastructure for all-solid-state battery development
abstract: Materials discovery increasingly depends on a multiscale ecosystem of simulations, experiments, and shared facilities, yet advances in individual AI tools do not by themselves connect the decisions that link these components. This gap is especially severe in all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs), whose development couples electrochemical performance to interfacial stability, mechanics, processing, manufacturability, reliability, safety, and cost.

title: Self-Derived Metal/Oxide Interface Engineering via Active Nitrogen Mediation
abstract: Self-derived phase engineering of metal oxides offers a powerful route to create interfaces without introducing foreign metallic elements, yet achieving systematic control over phase transition remains challenging. Here, active nitrogen-mediated phase engineering was demonstrated across various metal oxides (SnO 2 , ZnO, and TiO 2 ). As a model biphasic material, Sn/SnO 2 was investigated where urea thermolysis enabled the progressive formation of metallic Sn while largely preserving the host structure, allowing the Sn0 fraction to be systematically controlled.

title: The Thiolate Shell as a Dynamic Gold Reservoir: Size-Dependent Thermal Restructuring of Gold Nanoclusters from MACE-Based Machine-Learning Molecular Dynamics
abstract: Atomically precise thiolate-protected gold nanoclusters are used in catalysis, sensing and nanomedicine, where thermal activation, reaction conditions or local heating can change their atomic structure. Whether the gold–thiolate shell remains a fixed protective layer at elevated temperature, or takes part in the restructuring of the cluster, is still an open question, because first-principles molecular dynamics is limited to small clusters and short times.

title: Integrating classical similarity and multitask neural representations
abstract: Background. Computational prediction of compound–target associations can help prioritize hypotheses for experimental investigation. While deep learning architectures are increasingly proposed, their apparent superiority often relies on comparisons against untuned classical baselines or evaluation protocols prone to data leakage. Objective. We present a scaffold-disjoint evaluation benchmark derived from ChEMBL 37 to evaluate multitask neural representations against tuned classical similarity search, and we investigate whether combining both paradigms yields improved ranking performance.

title: Mechanistic Insights into Ascorbate-Mediated Activation of Pt(IV) Prodrugs: Axial-Ligand Modulation of Dissociative Reduction Pathways and Redox Latency
abstract: Pt(IV) coordination compounds act as anticancer prodrugs that are intracellularly reduced to cytotoxic Pt(II) species, a process whose selectivity and kinetics depend critically on the nature of the axial leaving (L L ) and bridging (L B ) ligands. Using DFT/IEFPCM calculations in water, we examined the ascorbate-mediated reduction of six [PtIV(NH 3 ) 2 Cl 2 (L L )(L B )] complexes bearing different axial-ligand combinations of chloride, bromide, and dichloroacetate (DCA): L L /L B = Br/Cl, Cl/Cl, DCA/Cl, as well as DCA/Br, Cl/Br, and Br/Br.

title: LigandFF: an open-source implementation of rule-based atom typing, charge assignment and parameter assignment by analogy
abstract: The CHARMM General Force Field (CGenFF) covers drug-like molecules through an automated assignment program that types atoms, assigns charges from bond-charge increments, and transfers missing bonded parameters from analogous ones with an associated penalty. The algorithms are published, but the program and its two hand-built rule files are distributed only in binary form. We describe LigandFF, an open-source reimplementation built exclusively from the published algorithms and the public CGenFF 5.0 topology, parameter and charge-increment files.

title: Weak-Form Regression Recovers the Delayed-Fluorescence Rate Law from Flash-Lamp Decays with Near-Optimal Precision
abstract: Delayed-fluorescence rates and their temperature laws are how thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) materials are ranked, yet the rate law is usually fixed before the analysis, and flash-lamp decays mix the emission with the excitation profile. We show that weak-form regression, with photon-counting statistics and the excitation built into its features, identifies the rate law as a sequence of linear problems with calibrated uncertainties.

title: Measured Host Optical Constants Shift Deep-Blue OLED Outcoupling by up to 14% (Relative) While Leaving the Stack Design Intact
abstract: Outcoupling designs for organic light-emitting diodes rest on the complex refractive index of every layer, yet host films are often given a constant index without absorption. We show what measured constants change, and what they do not. Variable-angle spectroscopic ellipsometry of three deep-blue phosphine-oxide host films (S1, S3 and S4), refitted from the raw data with several dispersion models, pins the index of the S1 and S4 films to a model-andspot spread of about ±0.002 (about ±0.004 at 95% once substrate-oxide, incidence-angle and roughness systematics are propagated) and reveals a…

title: Thermal Formation of a Magenta Merocyanine in Ethanol: A Microsolvated SP→TCC→TTC Pathway in a Nitrospiropyran
abstract: Solutions of 5’-methoxy-1’,3’,3’-trimethyl-6-nitrospiro[chromene-2,2’-indoline] in alcohols are intensely pink in the dark, become colorless under white light and recover their color thermally, with Arrhenius activation energies of 101.1± 0.5, 104.9± 1.6 and 105.3± 1.4 kJ mol−1 in ethanol, methanol and acidified ethanol, respectively. The measured process is therefore the thermal formation of the merocyanine (MC) from the photogenerated spiropyran (SP).

title: Scientific Symbiosis: Bridging Expertise and Fostering Effective Collaborations with Mass Spectrometrists
abstract: Mass spectrometry (MS) is increasingly used to answer biological questions, yet effective collaboration between mass spectrometrists and researchers in other fields can be limited by differences in terminology, expectations, and familiarity with analytical workflows. This review provides a practical and accessible guide to incorporating MS into biological and environmental research with an emphasis on improving communication and collaboration.

title: Reconfigurable Nanoscale Material Display
abstract: Dynamic material arrays that combine programmable reconfiguration with direct structural readout could enable materials that both adapt their spatial organization and represent molecular information. DNA nanotechnology offers exceptional control over nanoscale organization, yet most DNA-templated material arrays are static, whereas dynamic DNA circuits typically rely on indirect ensemble readouts.

title: Sulfur Oxidation State Controls Radical Smiles–Truce Rearrangements through a Switch in Cyclization Selectivity
abstract: The radical Smiles–Truce rearrangement is a powerful strategy for constructing aryl–carbon bonds, although competing ortho addition often limits the utility of conventional S(VI) sulfonamide precursors. Here, we demonstrate that switching to S(IV) sulfinamides enables selective ipso aryl migration while providing a stereochemical handle for asymmetric induction.

title: Physicochemical Prioritization of Hypothetical Metal–Organic Frameworks for Experimental Synthesis
abstract: The rapid expansion of AI-driven and computationally designed metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) raises a fundamental question: which hypothetical structures are most likely to be experimentally realized? Here, we develop a physicochemically informed strategy to prioritize MOFs for synthesis by integrating molecular synthetic accessibility, framework geometry, electronic structure, solvent removal stability, and thermodynamic stability through positive–unlabeled learning.

title: Jade1S SUMOylates tau and targets oligomers for degradation
abstract: The accumulation of insoluble tau aggregates is a pathological hallmark of tauopathies, including Alzheimer's disease. While molecular chaperones and clearance pathways regulate tau homeostasis, the mechanisms governing tau oligomerization and degradation remain incompletely defined. Recent genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have linked the JADE1 locus to tauopathy, and the PHD zinc finger protein Jade1S has been identified in complexes with tau in post-mortem brain tissue, prompting investigation into their biochemical relationship. Here, we characterize the reciprocal interactions between Jade1S and 0N4R tau stability and turnover. Covalent labeling mass spectrometry and co-immunoprecipitation mappings reveal that Jade1S binds wild-type 0N4R tau through redundant sites within its N-terminal and plant homeodomain (PHD) zinc finger domains. In vitro assays demonstrate that Jade1S functions as a SUMO E3 ligase, utilizing its PHD domains to mediate tau SUMOylation. Cell-based cycloheximide chase assays reveal a reciprocal stabilization dynamic: tau co-expression extends the overall physiological half-life of Jade1S from less than an hour to ~17 hours, arresting its turnover specifically within sarkosyl-insoluble fractions. Conversely, Jade1S selectively accelerates the degradation of sarkosyl-insoluble tau without altering the turnover of the soluble monomeric pool over chased time. Mechanistically, Jade1S redirects the clearance of SUMO2/3-modified tau oligomers away from basal autophagic-lysosomal pathways and toward proteasome-dependent degradation. Furthermore, Jade1S exhibits intrinsic molecular chaperone activity, inhibiting arachidonic acid-induced tau oligomerization in vitro. Together, these data characterize Jade1S as a dual-function SUMO ligase and chaperone that regulates tau stability, prevents oligomer assembly, and promotes the targeted proteasomal clearance of aggregated tau.

title: Archaeologists find direct evidence of cannabis use from 2,800 years ago
abstract: Human hair recovered from a prehistoric tomb contains cannabis chemicals

title: Half-integer quantum anomalous Hall effect in MnBi$_2$Te$_4$ via non-magnetic extension
abstract: Within an ab-initio approach, we study the electronic structure and Hall response of the antiferromagnetic topological insulator film of MnBi$_2$Te$_4$ in contact with non-magnetic GeBi$_2$Te$_4$ (Bi$_2$Te$_3$) overlayer. The proposed junction design eliminates the exchange splitting one of the Dirac cones of the MnBi$_2$Te$_4$ (0001) thus manifesting a half-integer quantum anomalous Hall phase. The described recipe allows to enlarge temperature of the effect observation, enriches the diversity of topological properties of the MnBi$_2$Te$_4$ compound and is appropriate for other layered antiferromagnetic topological insulators. Applying the proposed heterostructure design, the half-quantized Hall phase can be established with employing other overlayer and magnetic topological insulator films.

title: Nonlinear Interaction and Topological Selection Rules in two Skyrmion Merging: Emergence of Skyrmionium Textures
abstract: The nonlinear interaction of closely spaced magnetic skyrmions remains poorly understood, particularly the conditions governing their merger into a single skyrmion or a stable skyrmionium. Here, we investigate the merging dynamics of two Néel skyrmions using analytical modelling and micromagnetic simulations based on Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert dynamics. We examine the effects of exchange, Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction, anisotropy, and magnetostatic energies by varying the initial separation, polarity, winding number, and skyrmion size. Our results reveal a topological selection rule: skyrmions with identical polarity and opposite winding numbers form a stable skyrmionium at intermediate overlap, while all other configurations relax into a single skyrmion. We also identify a critical radius below which the skyrmionium collapses, showing that its formation requires both the appropriate topology and a minimum size. Energy analysis reveals that the transition involves cooperative relaxation of exchange frustration and redistribution of Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya and magnetostatic energies, leading to a double-domain-wall structure. The resulting skyrmionium exhibits persistent breathing oscillations around an equilibrium radius, confirming its dynamical stability as a metastable state. These findings establish a predictive framework for controlling skyrmion merging and provide design guidelines for engineering skyrmionium textures in chiral magnetic nanostructures.

title: A Passive Intelligent Metasurface: A Network Model
abstract: Intelligent metasurfaces enable advanced wave manipulation, including negative refraction, focusing, beam splitting and beam steering, with significant potential for practical applications. However, conventional approaches often rely on active metamaterials with gain, or demand computationally intensive solutions of inverse problems to find the optimal configuration. In this work, we use the scattering framework of quantum graph theory to derive an exact, analytic expression for configuration of a passive metasurface that produces a prescribed reflected wave field. The metasurface terminates a periodic lattice of waveguides and consists of an array of channels, each a tube of length $\ell_m$ ending in a vertex whose scattering parameter $λ_m$ sets how much of the wave is lost to the wall. For any prescribed incident and reflected field, the exact lengths and scattering parameters follow channel by channel, in closed form, from the ratio of the wave amplitudes returning to and leaving the lattice, and the metasurface is passive whenever this ratio does not exceed unity in modulus. We demonstrate the construction for both a one-dimensional and a two-dimensional metasurface. The one-dimensional metasurface terminates a two-dimensional lattice and steers, splits or perfectly absorbs Gaussian beams. The two-dimensional metasurface terminates a three-dimensional lattice and generates a prescribed image in a plane inside the lattice. In each case, we obtain the exact boundary properties that produce the effect.

title: Continuum Photonic Axion Insulators
abstract: Here, I study the conditions for realizing an axion topology in a homogeneous inversion-symmetric electromagnetic continuum, in the absence of a crystalline lattice. I introduce a continuum inversion invariant expressed solely in terms of the spectral properties of the material response in the zero- and infinite-wave-vector limits. Surprisingly, it is found that standard gyrotropic-type material responses are strongly constrained and, under fairly general conditions, cannot open an axion gap within first-order perturbation theory. Based on an analogy between the effective response of crystalline photonic axion insulators and the optical response of centrosymmetric altermagnets, a class of spatially dispersive odd magnetoelectric couplings that can open an axion gap is identified. These findings suggest an interesting hierarchy of nonreciprocal mechanisms in electromagnetic continua: while uniform gyrotropy relates to Chern phases, odd magnetoelectric coupling relates to axion phases.

title: Aptamers enable a distinct mode of conformational DNA recognition
abstract: Watson–Crick base-pairing defines the classical paradigm of nucleic-acid interactions, but growing research reveals noncanonical modes beyond this framework. Here we uncover a mode of interactions by which two DNA strands associate through a ligand-induced conformational rearrangement. Upon binding a small molecule, a structure-switching primary aptamer folds into a conformation that exposes a previously inaccessible docking interface. An independently evolved secondary aptamer recognizes this interface primarily through noncanonical interactions rather than sequence complementarity, reporting the ligand-bound state of the primary aptamer. This interaction is conformation-sensitive: single base-pair changes in the primary aptamer modulate secondary aptamer recognition. Across four chemically distinct small-molecule targets—serotonin, dopamine, testosterone and deoxycorticosterone 21-glucoside—secondary aptamers were identified for three, and the serotonin system was translated into surface-based sandwich assays. These results demonstrate that a ligand-induced conformational state, rather than sequence complementarity or the chemical identity of the ligand, can serve as the epitope for nucleic-acid recognition, expanding the molecular features that DNA can be evolved to detect.

title: XTQSPRKinetic: A Mixture-of-Experts Framework for Reaction-Space Clustering and Property Learning from SMILES
abstract: Chemical heterogeneity can limit the ability of a single global structure–property model to represent modified Arrhenius parameters across a reaction network. XTQSPRKinetic combines learned reaction grouping with specialist regression in a configurable mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture evaluated on a Reaction Mechanism Generator (RMG)-derived n-hexane pyrolysis/steam-cracking network containing 1215 elementary reactions.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Dopant-Dependent Surface Interaction Modulation by Pt with Hexagonal Perovskites for Robust Bifunctional Oxygen Electrocatalysts in Rechargeable Zn−Air Batteries
abstract: Rechargeable Zn−air batteries (ZABs) have attracted considerable attention as promising energy storage systems owing to their high theoretical energy density and environmental compatibility. However, their practical application is hindered by the sluggish ORR/OER kinetics at the air cathode. This study investigates low Pt-modified Fe- and Ni-doped hexagonal perovskites (BaTi0.8M0.2O3−δ, M = Fe and Ni) as robust bifunctional oxygen electrocatalysts, focusing on the modulation of their participating metal and electronic structures.

title: A Cationic Ruthenium Olefin Metathesis Catalyst Supported on Weakly Coordinating Silica
abstract: Silica functionalized with Lewis acidic silylium aluminate ion-pairs ([iPr3Si][(RFO)3Al–OSi≡] (RF = C(CF3)3)) abstract chloride from the second-generation Grubbs-Hoveyda catalyst (SIMes)Cl2Ru=CH(o-iPrO-C6H4) (GH-II) to form supported [(SIMes)ClRu=CH(o-iPrO-C6H4)][(RFO)3Al–OSi≡] (1) and iPr3SiCl. Solid-state NMR measurements at 100 K, desorption of Ru from the support, and X-ray adsorption spectroscopy (XAS) are consistent with formation of a monomeric Ru-benzylidene cation that is electrostatically immobilized on the modified silica surface.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Direct calculation of dipole moment surfaces through second-order symmetry-adapted perturbation theory for properties
abstract: Interaction-induced dipole moment surfaces are vital for calculating line intensities and collision-induced absorption coefficients for van der Waals complexes. We introduce the perturbative corrections, of second order with respect to the interaction operator, to the dipole moment (or, in general, any one-electron property) change due to noncovalent interactions. These are obtained in the spirit of the symmetry-adapted perturbation theory for properties (propSAPT) method, developed recently by some of us [B. Tyrcha et al., JCTC 21(9), 4562--4578 (2025)]. When orbital relaxation effects due to the external property field are properly introduced, these can be understood as analytical derivatives of the second-order SAPT interaction energies. We apply the newly introduced formalism to calculations of dipole moment surfaces for three light van der Waals complexes: He...Ar, He...H$_2$ and the H$_2$ dimer. The propSAPT method is compared against finite-field SAPT calculations and finite-field supermolecular CCSD(T) as the reference.

title: Towards Multiscale Molecular Representation Learning through Geometry-Based Fragmentation for Polymer Property Prediction
abstract: It is well established that molecular substructures can contribute unequally to chemical and physical properties, with specific motifs or side chains often playing dominant roles. Fragment-based representations have therefore emerged as an effective strategy for incorporating chemically meaningful inductive biases, as exemplified by molecular fingerprints and fragment-based attention mechanisms. However, many existing fragmentation-based machine learning methods rely on predefined chemical rules, which may yield suboptimal fragmentation for previously unseen or chemically unfamiliar structures and often overlook the importance of multiscale molecular representations. To address these limitations, we formulate molecular fragmentation as a radius-constrained optimization problem inspired by the k-center formulation, where the number of clusters is not fixed a priori but emerges from the specified radius, and propose a geometry-based fragmentation method that partitions arbitrary molecular or material structures using largely geometric information, without relying on predefined chemical fragmentation rules. The method provides flexible control over fragment size, enabling the construction of multiscale fragment representations for scale-adaptive modeling. Building on this framework, we develop a geometric fragment-based attention mechanism that integrates multiscale structural information and incorporate it into a multimodal machine learning model combining p-SMILES representations with three-dimensional (3D) conformational information. Experiments on a benchmark polymer dataset show that incorporating 3D conformational information improves prediction accuracy for several properties over models based exclusively on p-SMILES representations. Explainable artificial intelligence analyses further provide insights into the physical relevance of the learned representations.

title: Technohybridism: Recursive Semantic Normalization in AI-Mediated Societies
abstract: Language-generating AI systems are no longer only objects of linguistic interaction: their outputs increasingly re-enter the communicative and institutional practices from which their training material was drawn. Drawing on social theory, social epistemology, and the philosophy of language, this article develops a sociotechnical account of that re-entry. We introduce recursive semantic normalization: the process through which machine-generated formulations, once recurrently taken up, evaluated, reused, and institutionally retained, participate in the reproduction and transformation of semantic regularities. Under the heading of technohybridism, we argue that the relevant unit of analysis is the hybrid semantic system, a recursively coupled configuration of human practices, computational generation, and institutional uptake. First, we distinguish the concept from neighbouring accounts, including model collapse, looping effects, machine habitus, machine culture, and the epistemology of AI testimony. Second, we develop an analytical model that separates generation, selection, uptake, and persistence and distinguishes machine-attributable change from change that would have occurred anyway. Third, we analyse uptake as routinized, institutionally diffused, and socially stratified practice and state conditions under which machine-derived regularities become norms. Fourth, we identify social-epistemic consequences: the laundering of provenance that weakens epistemic vigilance, the erosion of the cognitive diversity on which collective inquiry depends, and the narrowing of shared hermeneutical resources. An evidential ladder for empirical research follows. The account attributes no normative authority to machine outputs; what changes is the field within which human and institutional uptake operates.

title: Pressure-Induced Phase Transition and Superconducting Properties of LiPdH$_2$: A First-Principles Study
abstract: We present a detailed first-principles investigation of the superconducting hydride LiPdH$_2$, focusing on the competition between its tetragonal $P4/mmm$ and rhombohedral $R\bar{3}m$ phases. Our results reveal a pressure-induced phase transition near 220 GPa, where $R\bar{3}m$ overtakes $P4/mmm$ in thermodynamic stability. The $R\bar{3}m$ phase is predicted to be superconducting, with $T_{\rm c}$ values of up to 46 K in the harmonic approximation and 28 K at the anharmonic level. In contrast, although the $P4/mmm$ phase is stable up to 200 GPa, it maintains a more rigid electronic character with weaker hydrogen involvement, resulting in lower superconducting performance. Ionic quantum and anharmonic effects play a decisive role in stabilizing $P4/mmm$ and shaping its superconducting properties, whereas these effects diminish rapidly with pressure. These findings highlight the interplay between structural stability, hydrogen orbital activity, and quantum effect in optimizing the superconductivity of hydrogen-based superconductors.

title: Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning
abstract: Knowledge of the hidden interior structure of an object, including the presence and location of cavities, is essential for predictive simulation, robotic manipulation, and nondestructive inspection. However, such cavities leave no direct signature on the static visible surface, making collision-induced deformation one of the few cues used to infer their presence. Structure from Collision (SfC) addresses this problem by recovering the hidden interior structure of an object from multiview observations of a collision event. SfC is challenging for two reasons: hidden cavities are only indirectly observable through surface motion, and voids correspond to the absence of material, making direct optimization using standard density representations difficult. The density-based SfC baseline inherits both difficulties. Surface-matching gradients do not directly indicate the cavity location, while density gradients can be weak or uninformative inside or near void regions. Therefore, we reformulate SfC as hypothesis-space reasoning, representing hidden cavities as explicit structural hypotheses whose variables encode available structural assumptions rather than relying on implicit density updates. A global stage performs gradient-free optimization over this hypothesis space using forward-only material point method (MPM) simulation. A local stage then refines the selected hypothesis as a Lagrangian particle system through gradient-based optimization using differentiable MPM simulation. On the SfC benchmark, our method improves hidden-structure reconstruction and future prediction over the density-based SfC baseline. Interior-topology stress tests and robustness analyses characterize its scope and limitations. The project page is available at https://www.kecl.ntt.co.jp/people/kaneko.takuhiro/projects/sfc-hypothesis/.

title: ChemE-as-Code: An Open-Source Platform for Agentic AI in Chemical Engineering
abstract: ChemE-as-Code provides an open-source environment in which AI agents built on large language models (LLMs) can carry out chemical engineering work and engineers can check it. Its calculation tools range from catalysis through process simulation to plant layout, HAZOP and life cycle assessment, and skills tell a general-purpose agent how to use them. Engineering files are linked, machine-readable and versioned in Git; calculations run outside the LLM, each value records its origin, and automated checks report inconsistencies and out-of-date results by file and line. In an illustrative ammonia case, agents developed a written task into a preliminary basic-engineering package (simulation files, P&IDs, layout, HAZOP, datasheets, relief) for USD 224 of API cost in the design sessions. Planted faults and engineering changes show that the checks find what their rules cover and miss the rest, so they guide human review rather than replace it. No independent engineer has reviewed the design.

title: A sweeter future? AI helps scientists discover new sugar substitutes
abstract: Researchers Dr. Shayma El-Atawneh and professor Amiram Goldblum at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem have developed a new computational framework that identified 92 promising candidates for future sugar substitutes from more than 50 million chemical compounds. The study, published in the journal Food Chemistry, demonstrates how artificial intelligence and molecular modeling could accelerate the discovery of new sweeteners while helping overcome one of the industry's persistent challenges: unwanted bitter aftertastes.

title: Mechanical adaptation drives out-of-equilibrium network reorganization and self-strengthening in adapt-ring networks
abstract: Adapt-ring networks consisting of dense, reconfigurable α-cyclodextrin crystalline domains and sparsely crosslinked polyethylene glycol form adaptive polymer materials that remodel and strengthen in response to mechanical stress.

title: Multiscale Molecular Simulations Reveal the Structural Pathway of Histatin 1 Self-Association
abstract: Histatins are a family of human saliva peptides; the three main members consist of Histatin 1 (Hst1), Histatin 3 (Hst3), and Histatin 5 (Hst5). Despite their high primary-structure similarity, the peptides display varied functions and behaviors. Experimental evidence supports concentration-dependent self-association of Hst1, but the molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. This property is of interest because it is not observed in Hst5. Here, we combine atomistic and coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations with a decomposition-based trajectory analysis to investigate the structural origins of Hst1 self-association across multiple length and time scales. Atomistic simulations reveal dimers that remain associated over the simulated time scales, together with transient higher-order oligomers. Analysis of intermolecular residue contacts highlights aromatic residues as prominent contributors to peptide association, consistent with a multivalent interaction network. Coarse-grained simulations extend these observations to larger systems and longer time scales, demonstrating a progressive assembly into dynamic peptide clusters. By discretizing the resulting conformational landscape, we extracted representative structures to reconstruct the self-association pathway from dispersed monomers to higher-order assemblies. The simulations provide a multiscale description of Hst1 self-association and support a model in which weak, multivalent peptide–peptide contacts contribute to the formation of dynamic peptide-rich assemblies. Although the present work does not directly demonstrate liquid–liquid phase separation, it identifies molecular features associated with biomolecular assembly.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Structural basis for inefficient G protein coupling by Frizzled receptors
abstract: Frizzleds (FZDs) are class F G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) that primarily signal through Dishevelled (DVL) to initiate Wnt signalling, with evidence for context-specific coupling to heterotrimeric G proteins. Every FZD-G protein structure to date has been determined without an agonist, implying that agonist binding is not required for stable complex formation in vitro and directly contradicting the difficulty of demonstrating G protein coupling in cells. All these structures contain unassigned density between the receptor and the heterotrimeric G protein. From structures generated by single-particle cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) of FZD7-Gs and FZD5-Gq, we identify this density as the detergent lauryl maltose neopentyl glycol (LMNG), which bridges the receptor and G protein to stabilise a weak, shallow interface. Absence of LMNG - in biochemical preparations and molecular dynamics simulations - destabilises the complex, showing that constitutive FZD-G protein engagement is intrinsically weak. The weak G protein coupling is governed by a conserved intracellular interface that when mutated differentially influences DVL and G protein signalling. Our findings show that LMNG has masked the instability of purified FZD-G protein complexes and provide the structural basis of FZDs as inherently weak G protein activators that are predisposed to DVL signalling.

title: Programmable Directional Assembly of Hydrogen-Bonded Lead Organic Chalcogenolates
